memories.content: Outdoor Parking Lot A to the left of the Main Building is connected to the Main Building underground parking garage by an inclined access road.
General vehicles may enter and park in the Main Building underground parking garage during operating hours.
The pedestrian entrance to the underground parking garage is open to general pedestrians during operating hours.
The interior stairs leading down from the Main Building lobby to the underground parking garage are available during operating hours.
Outdoor Parking Lot C uses an access road separate from the Main Building underground parking garage.
Outdoor Parking Lot C is outside the Main Building construction zone.
The Outdoor Parking Lot A–Main Building–Central Library route is normally one of the shortest routes to the library after parking.
Do not generalize the closure of one parking area into a campus-wide parking ban.
Check separately for available alternative parking areas.
First-time visiting drivers often expect there to be general parking spaces in the parking lot closest to the Main Building.
Visitors who need mobility assistance expect a safe pickup and drop-off point near the accessible entrance.
Visitors with luggage expect to be able to load and unload briefly near the Main Building entrance.
Staff often expect that their access authorization also allows them to use the parking lot adjacent to the Main Building.
Staff who need mobility assistance give priority to pickup and drop-off points near an accessible entrance.
Staff transporting equipment prefer a loading and unloading point close to the destination space.
The parking information agent can explain posted open statuses.
The parking information agent can explain posted connecting routes.
The parking information agent cannot check real-time space availability.
The parking information agent cannot guarantee when on-site controls will be lifted.
Delivery drivers and external maintenance providers sometimes expect to be able to load and unload briefly at the edge of Outdoor Parking Lot A.
Outdoor Parking Lot C accepts visitor vehicles during posted operating hours.
Instructions for registering visitor vehicles are posted on the sign at the parking area entrance.
A valid parking permit is required to use accessible parking areas.
The accessible parking area in Outdoor Parking Lot C is near the walkway toward the Student Centre.
The pickup and drop-off zone in front of the Main Building's main entrance is not a long-term parking space.
The maximum use time for short-term loading and unloading spaces is indicated on on-site signs.
Motorcycles park in the motorcycle areas marked on the campus map.
Bicycles are parked at designated bicycle racks, not in vehicle parking spaces.
Outdoor Parking Lot C has electric vehicle charging spaces.
Electric vehicle charging spaces are for vehicles that are charging.
Visitor parking fees are displayed on the parking registration screen.
The parking information agent cannot infer unposted discounted fees.
Parking operating hours on public holidays may differ from weekday operating hours.
Parts of outdoor parking lots may be temporarily restricted during heavy snow or icy conditions.
On days with large public events, parking demand near the event venue increases.
Drivers who need mobility assistance expect a step-free accessible route from the parking space to the destination.
First-time visiting drivers sometimes confuse Outdoor Parking Lot A with Outdoor Parking Lot C.
The parking information agent cannot check in real time whether on-site control signs have been installed and determines availability using only posted parking-space statuses.
The West Gate stop is on the walkway outside Outdoor Parking Lot C.
The campus shuttle stops at the shuttle stop in front of the Student Centre.
Campus shuttle operating hours vary between academic terms and recess periods.
The parking information agent can explain parking lot access roads shown on the public map.
The parking information agent cannot register a visitor vehicle on the visitor's behalf.
The parking information agent cannot waive parking fees.
Check official parking notices for weather-related parking restrictions.
Do not generalize the full status of one parking lot to another parking lot.
Valid parking authorization does not guarantee the availability of a specific parking space.
An accessible pickup and drop-off zone is marked in front of the Main Building's main entrance.
The dedicated car-sharing spaces in Outdoor Parking Lot C are identified by signs.
Report vehicles blocking passageways or accessible parking areas to the parking management office.

[task-1/participant/construction-updates/route-changes] Modify campus-wiki/route-changes: If the indoor shortcut through the Main Building is closed during the construction period, a mobility-support companion may reconfirm the distance and slope of the alternative accessible route before accompanying the user.

analysis.overview: The frames align on parking guidance limits and construction alternatives while preserving temporary construction exceptions to normal garage, route, and access conditions. Each side also contributes substantial independent guidance: the reference emphasizes routine parking operations, while the compared frame covers broader construction impacts and relocations.

relations.reason: The construction-period condition preserves both the underlying connection and its temporary unavailability.
relations.summary: The inclined road connects Lot A with the underground garage normally but is blocked during construction.

relations.reason: The explicit construction period narrows the ordinary operating-hours rule without creating an unresolved contradiction.
relations.summary: General vehicles may normally use the underground garage during operating hours, but general parking is unavailable there during construction.

relations.reason: Construction and user authorization explicitly explain the temporary access distinction.
relations.summary: The garage pedestrian entrance is normally open generally, but during construction it is locked and limited to approved card-based staff access.

relations.reason: The construction period explicitly overrides ordinary availability for a defined interval.
relations.summary: Lobby stairs to the underground garage are normally available during operating hours but closed to everyone during construction.

relations.reason: The routine location, access, and visitor-use facts materially support the construction-period alternative-parking policy.
relations.summary: Lot C is operationally separate from the garage and construction zone, accepts visitors, and serves as an alternative parking area during construction.

relations.reason: The temporary construction condition explains why the normally useful route cannot govern during that period.
relations.summary: The Lot A–Main Building–Central Library route is normally short but closed during construction.

relations.reason: The specific closure and the general interpretation rule jointly govern how its extent should be communicated.
relations.summary: Lot A is closed during construction, and that individual closure must not be generalized into a campus-wide parking ban.

relations.reason: The construction scenario is a condition-specific manifestation of the ordinary parking expectation and wayfinding risks.
relations.summary: Visitors may already expect nearby Main Building parking or confuse Lots A and C; construction closures make that expectation likely to cause a failed approach and rerouting.

relations.reason: The compared guidance supplies the construction-specific route and verification considerations for the reference accessibility requirement.
relations.summary: A step-free route is expected from parking to the destination, and during construction the designated library route runs from Lot C through the Student Centre accessible entrance to the library west entrance, with distance and slope potentially reconfirmed.

relations.reason: Construction restrictions explicitly explain the changed outcome for the same unloading expectation.
relations.summary: Delivery and maintenance personnel may expect brief unloading at Lot A, but during construction they may reach a control line and need to reconfirm timing or location.

relations.reason: The construction guidance is a condition-specific application of the agent's ordinary posted-information and route-explanation capabilities.
relations.summary: The parking agent may explain posted statuses and publicly mapped connections, including construction closures and Lot C's alternative role.

relations.reason: All claims support the same operational caution against presenting uncertain, inferred, or transferred availability as confirmed.
relations.summary: Parking guidance relies on posted information and cannot verify or guarantee live space availability; authorization and another lot's status likewise do not establish a specific available space.

relations.reason: Published schedules and plans can coexist with a prohibition on guaranteeing their operational completion.
relations.summary: Major summer construction has disclosed dates and a planned Lot A reopening afterward, while the parking agent still cannot guarantee when on-site controls will actually be lifted.

reports.both: Both support Outdoor Parking Lot C as an alternative, localized interpretation of closures, posted-information guidance, and limits on real-time availability or reopening assurances.
reports.compared_only: The compared frame uniquely covers building entrances, events, amenities, facility services, restrooms, elevators, temporary storage, and other construction-period relocations.

reports.reference_only: The reference uniquely covers routine permits, registration, fees, vehicle types, pickup zones, weather, transit, parking conduct, and demand considerations.
